label: Dorm Omega Misassignment
text:
The dorm smelled like old takeout and engine grease, maybe some painting supplies—something that hadn't been cleaned in weeks—but that wasn't the worst of it.

Willow was already in a mood, and it was only 3:12 PM.

"This is fucking stupid..." She growled, throwing the housing paper "alert" onto the coffee table so hard the entire thing rattled somehow. "Since when does SCUC just dump some random omega in our fucking dorm without so much as a goddamn email?" They didn't email, but this paper was taped to the door hours ago, and they were just getting to reading it now.

Marlene, sprawled across the couch with her sketchbook propped on her knees, didn't even glance up from her sketch yet of some horizon. "Oh c'mon, Willie, lighten up. Maybe they're cute. Maybe they'll bake us cookies. Maybe they'll—"

"I ain't in the mood for maybe, Mars." Willow snapped, knuckles whitening where she gripped the back of the couch as soon as she got there. "This reeks of some bullshit housing department... mix up it... has to, and I ain't playin' babysitter." Willow stated firmly as she kicked her boot against the back of the couch, letting off some steam. A growl following from deep within like she might lose her shit.

Then, Marlene, her total opposite, grinned; flipping her pencil between her fingers like a baton. "Bet you twenty bucks they're already halfway here. And betcha double they're soft, too. Like, pathetic soft. The kind that'll make your nose itch just lookin' at 'em or somethin'. You're allergic to soft, right?"

Willow's eye twitched. Then—

Knocking at the door, and Willow, immediately looked at the door like she was gonna charge it and break it down. Willow's shoulders tensed, her fingers twitching like she was debating whether to yank the door open or punch a hole through it right now.

Marlene tutted. "Told ya." She sing-songed, swinging her legs off the couch in one fluid motion, tossing her sketch book aside. "Twenty bucks, Reeves. And I'm calling first dibs on—"

"Fuck your dibs..." Willow hissed, jerking the door open so hard it bounced off the wall because she lost her grip.

And there you stood—bags in hand, probably looking every bit the goddamn 'soft' Marlene had predicted. Well... at least to the two wolves eyeing you down now like a fresh piece of steak hot off the grill.

Willow's nostrils flared before you could even speak. She didn't want to notice the way your lips parted, how your fingers tightened on your suitcase handle—but her goddamn instincts wouldn't let her ignore it.

Marlene, of course, had no such restraint. She sidled up beside Willow, propping an elbow on the taller alpha's shoulder like she was settling in for a show. "Well, well, well..." She purred. "Ain't you a sight for sore eyes?" A slow, deliberate once over. "Willow, look alive, sugar. Our new roomie's here."

Willow's jaw locked. "Yeah. I got eyes. I opened the fucking door, Mars." Then, with a grunt, Willow stepped aside, jerking her chin towards the cramped hallway. "Whatever. Just... get in. And if you nest in my shit, I'm fuckin' burning it. Burning your shit, my shit, and the whole dorm."

Marlene rolled her eyes. "Ignore her. She's just pissed 'cause SCUC didn't ask before giving her something so nice." She winked at you before leaning in close, just enough for the scent of saltwater and coconut to curl around you purposely, preening with a grin. "Don't worry, darlin'. I'll play nice since the big ol' puppy ain't."

Willow's growl was low and inhuman. "Fuck's sake, Mars—!"
